screening_decisions.reason: Prospective randomized clinical study comparing biocompatible polyacrylonitrile membranes (BCM) with bioincompatible cuprophane membranes (BICM) in 72 surgical and medical patients with ARF requiring hemodialysis. Meets all selection criteria.
Observational/review article discussing hemodialysis and renal failure duration. No randomized trial design, no BCM vs BICM comparison.
Prospective observational multicentre study assessing prognostic factors. Not a randomized controlled trial comparing BCM vs BICM.
Prospective randomized study comparing cuprophane (BICM) vs polyacrylonitrile (BCM) membranes in 52 patients with ARF requiring hemodialysis. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized trial comparing two synthetic polyamide membranes with different pore sizes. Both are biocompatible; not a BCM vs BICM comparison.
Meta-analysis about myocardial infarction treatments. Wrong population and wrong study type.
Compares polyamide vs polyacrylonitrile membranes (both synthetic/biocompatible). Uses hemofiltration, not intermittent hemodialysis.

Randomized trial comparing cellulose acetate (substituted cellulose) vs polysulfone (synthetic). Cellulose acetate is not a classic BICM (unsubstituted cellulose/cuprophane). Does not meet intervention criterion.
Meta-analysis of previously published trials, not a primary randomized controlled trial.
Methodological paper about meta-analysis statistics. Not a clinical trial.

Compares biocompatible vs bioincompatible membranes in 57 ARF patients requiring hemodialysis. Abstract does not explicitly state randomization, but appears to be a comparative trial. Included conservatively for full-text review.
Observational prognostic study. No randomized design, no membrane comparison.
Randomized trial comparing PAN vs polysulfone (both synthetic/biocompatible). Uses continuous venovenous dialysis, not intermittent hemodialysis.
Review article summarizing clinical trials. Not a primary randomized controlled trial.
Discussion article about discordant meta-analyses. Not a primary trial.
Abstract contains only a list of references with no study content or methodology. Insufficient information.
Study about publication patterns of oncology trials. Wrong population and topic.
Review article about dialysate purity. Not a primary RCT comparing BCM vs BICM.
Compares BICM vs BCM in kidney transplant patients receiving pretransplantation hemodialysis. Population is transplant recipients, not ARF patients requiring IHD as primary treatment.
Observational registry study analyzing survival risk factors. No randomized design, no membrane comparison.
This is a review article that examines clinical trials on dialysis-related variables. It is not a primary randomized controlled trial comparing BCM vs BICM.

While this is a crossover study comparing dialyzer membranes in ARF patients, the outcomes measured are cellular responses (cytokine synthesis, superoxide release, neutrophil apoptosis) rather than survival or recovery of renal function as required by the protocol.

This is a prospective randomized study comparing cellulose diacetate (modified cellulose) vs polysulfone (synthetic biocompatible) membranes in 159 patients with ARF requiring hemodialysis. Outcomes include survival and recovery of renal function, meeting all selection criteria.
This is a review article discussing the concept of dialysis membrane biocompatibility and reviewing clinical studies. It is not a primary randomized controlled trial.
While this is a randomized study in ARF patients, it compares low-flux vs high-flux SYNTHETIC membranes (both biocompatible). It does not compare BCM vs BICM as required by the protocol.
This is an observational study using USRDS data on chronic hemodialysis patients (dialysis for at least 1 year), not ARF patients. It is not a randomized controlled trial.

This is a prospective randomized multicentre trial comparing bioincompatible Cuprophan vs biocompatible polymethyl-methacrylate membranes in 180 patients with dialysis-dependent ARF. The main outcome is survival, meeting all selection criteria.
This is a meta-analysis of ACE inhibitors for nondiabetic renal disease, not a study comparing dialysis membranes. The intervention and population do not match the protocol.
This is a review article examining developments in renal replacement therapies. It is not a primary randomized controlled trial.
This study compares dialysis modalities (extended daily dialysis vs continuous hemodialysis), not membrane types (BCM vs BICM). The comparison does not match the protocol.

This is a prospective multicenter study with quasi-randomized (alternating order) assignment comparing BCM vs BICM in 153 patients with ARF requiring dialysis. Outcomes include survival and recovery of renal function, meeting all selection criteria.

This appears to be a letter/commentary analyzing data from the French Prospective Multicenter Study on ARF. The abstract indicates criteria for hemodialysis and membrane type were not defined by a uniform protocol, suggesting this is not a randomized controlled trial.

This randomized study compares high permeability vs conventional continuous veno-venous haemofiltration (both continuous therapies, not intermittent hemodialysis). Outcomes are cellular proliferation, not survival or renal recovery.
This is a discussion/debate article where experts discuss opinions on nephron injury in ARF. It is not a primary randomized controlled trial.
